task_name: Milepost Driving Academy - Scenario clip training library
client_brief:
Milepost needs short training examples for the listed driving scenarios. Show the manoeuvre clearly enough that a nervous learner can follow the necessary stages, with narration and labels that agree with the approved instruction. The upright example must keep the relevant road context visible. Do not turn a disconnected set of road shots into apparent evidence of a completed manoeuvre. Adequate scenario footage and cleared narration are prerequisites, not something the editor should guess.

Deliverables
1. Driving-scenario training clip: 8 named exports. The manoeuvre is shown without omitting a necessary stage. The narration matches the visual scenario. The instruction agrees with the cleared training copy.
2. Vertical training example: 1 named export. The relevant road context remains visible. The complete instruction is intelligible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. Speech-led work requires supplied or explicitly authorised synthetic speech; do not invent documentary speech.
- Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live-action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Driver education and road safety training (accredited in car and classroom academy)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009 in Burlington, Vermont. Small: two instructors, roughly sixty learners a term.
brand_identity.about: Milepost is an accredited driving academy in Vermont running in car lessons and a classroom course. Two instructors, about sixty learners a term, mostly sixteen to nineteen with a steady number of adult beginners. Our reputation is that we are calm and thorough, and every learner leaves certain about what they are looking at. Everything we make has to earn the trust of a nervous learner and the parent paying for the course.
brand_identity.audience: Learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. People who want reassurance that the school is careful and legitimate.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, accredited and dependable. Sixty dollars an hour. Not a budget app, not a premium driving experience brand.
brand_identity.typography: A plain, highly legible system: a clear humanist sans for titles and step lists, set generously, with a neutral companion for call outs and captions. Legibility at small size in a printed guide and on a phone is the whole criterion. Nothing expressive or condensed.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
brand_identity.values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Lane changes

values.Steps: 1. Check your interior mirror for what is behind you. 2. Check the door mirror on the side you are moving to. 3. Signal in good time. 4. Take a quick glance over your shoulder to clear the blind spot. 5. Move across smoothly in one steady movement. 6. Cancel the signal and settle into the new lane.
values.Callout: One lane at a time. Never two at once.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Right turns

values.Steps: 1. Slow down early and get into the correct position. 2. Signal right in good time. 3. Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into. 4. Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane. 5. Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Left turns across traffic

values.Steps: 1. Begin slowing well before the junction. 2. Move to the correct position near the centre line. 3. Signal left across the oncoming lane in good time. 4. Stop at the give-way line if you cannot see a clear gap. 5. Watch the oncoming traffic and judge the gaps, not the cars. 6. Look through the turn to where you want to end up. 7. Check for pedestrians crossing the road you are entering. 8. Wait for a gap you are certain of, not one you are hoping for. 9. When the gap is clear, turn smoothly across the lane. 10. Keep your wheels straight while you wait so a knock will not push you forward. 11. Complete the turn into your own lane and cancel the signal.
values.Callout: When in doubt, wait. A missed gap costs seconds; a wrong one costs more.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Roundabouts

values.Steps: 1. Read the signs and road markings on the approach. 2. Slow down early and choose your lane before you arrive. 3. Give way to traffic already on the roundabout, usually from your left. 4. Wait for a gap and enter without stopping if you can. 5. Keep to your lane and follow the markings round. 6. Signal left as you pass the exit before the one you want. 7. Leave the roundabout in your lane and check your mirror.
values.Callout: Look left, take your time, and keep moving when it is clear.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Parallel parking

values.Steps: 1. Find a space at least a car and a half long. 2. Pull up level with the car in front, about half a metre out. 3. Check your mirrors and blind spot for anything coming. 4. Select reverse and begin backing slowly. 5. When your back wheels are level with the other car's bumper, turn the wheel toward the kerb. 6. Bring the car back at a shallow angle. 7. When the front clears the parked car, straighten the wheel. 8. Reverse gently until you are parallel with the kerb. 9. Adjust forward and back until you are centred in the space.
values.Callout: Slow and small. Let the wheel do the work.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Merging

values.Steps: 1. Build your speed along the slip road to match the traffic. 2. Check your mirrors as you go. 3. Look for a gap in the lane you are joining. 4. Signal to show where you are going. 5. Keep glancing between the road ahead and your mirror. 6. Ease into the gap at matching speed. 7. Do not stop on the slip road unless you have to. 8. Cancel your signal and keep a safe distance.
values.Callout: Match the speed, find the gap, ease in.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Four-way stops

values.Steps: 1. Come to a full stop at the line, every time. 2. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. 3. If two of you arrive together, the one on the right goes first. 4. When it is your turn, move off clearly so others know.
values.Callout: Full stop, then first come, first go.

deliverables.name: Driving-scenario training clip - Hazard recognition

values.Steps: 1. Keep scanning far ahead, not just the car in front. 2. Ask what could happen next and cover the brake. 3. Slow down before a hazard, not on top of it.
values.Callout: See it early, and you have time.
